{{Quote|I'm a ''cyborg'' now, more machine than man... and ''happy'' to cast my lot in ''with'' the machines! Leave ''me'' and my Droid World in ''peace!''|Kligson|<ref name="marvel47" />}}
'''Kligson''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] who ruled over [[Kligson's Moon/Legends|Kligson's Moon]], a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] made out of [[Starship/Legends|starship]] parts and inhabited solely by [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. A veteran of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and a [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] in the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], Kligson was marked for [[Death/Legends|death]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] after refusing to lead an invasion of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Sucharme]]. Kligson was rescued by the [[Grohl Liberation Front]] and received [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] enhancements that saved his life. Afterward, Kligson retreated entirely from contact with other organics, sequestering himself aboard his "Droid World" and only consorting with mechanicals.

Kligson became a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] legend in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to come, as word spread of a reclusive [[Technician/Legends|technician]] who could seemingly repair any droid. Kligson kept his moon out of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], only for the war to reach his doorstep in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], when a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] asked Kligson to examine a damaged [[Imperial warbot]]. That prompted a group of Imperial-sympathizing droids to launch a coup attempt against Kligson, although the cyborg's [[Kligson's faction|faction]] prevailed in the ensuing [[Kligson's Moon civil war|civil war]]. Afterward, Kligson retreated even further from organic contact.

==Biography==
===Lifelong warrior===
{{Quote|You're ''talking'' to Kligson, Rebel! And I suffered enough in the ''Clone Wars'' to make me hostile to my fellow organics ''forever!''|Kligson, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="marvel47" />}}
A native of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sucharme]], the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] known as Kligson grew up in an environment marked by war. As a young man, Kligson joined up with the [[Grohl Sector Defense Force]], reaching the rank of [[Major/Legends|Major]] and seeing action fighting [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] in the [[Grohl sector/Legends|Grohl sector's]] Rimward regions and intervening in the civil war on [[Ostega]]. Later, in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], native hostility to exploitative [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] business practices on Sucharme led to a full-scale Federation invasion. Kligson became one of the leaders of the [[Sucharmese resistance]], and after helping to drive the Trade Federation offworld, joined the Grohl Liberation Front and embarked on sabotage missions against Federation interests throughout his home sector.<ref name="EGWAC8" />

[[File:KligsonSide.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Kligson suffered grievous wounds during his time in the Imperial Army, leading to his rebuilding as a cyborg.]]
At some point during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Kligson came into contact with [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], who recruited the now-seasoned fighter to the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]''&mdash;a group of warriors enlisted to train [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC troopers]] and [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. However, itching to get back in the fight, Kligson soon enlisted in the Grand Army on his own, becoming one of the military force's few non-[[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Officer/Legends|officers]]. After seeing action on [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]] and [[Praesitlyn/Legends|Praesitlyn]] and surviving until the end of the war, Kligson remained with his [[Clone trooper/Legends|troops]] as the Grand Army became the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], becoming a [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] in the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].<ref name="EGWAC8" />

However, Kligson's career in Imperial service proved short. His new [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] soon sent Kligson back home to subjugate Sucharme in the Empire's name&mdash;a patriot, Kligson questioned his orders, and was immediately gunned down by his [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. Ironically, Kligson's life was saved by the very people he had been ordered to kill, when the Grohl Liberation Front launched a timely ambush and recovered their former brother-in-arms. The Grohl Liberation Front placed Kligson's barely-living remains in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] and placed him in a [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] body made out of [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droid]] parts, preserving his life by turning him into a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]].<ref name="EGWAC8" />

===Droid World===
{{Quote|There's an electronics genius named Kligson who could help us. He lives all alone on a place called Droid World. But the man's a bit strange, downright weird if you ask me.|A Rebel soldier to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="further">''[[The Further Adventures: Droid World]]''</ref>}}
[[File:KligsonsMoon-MSW47.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kligson's Moon, Kligson's most famous creation and his new home.]]
The Grohl Liberation Front had high hopes that Kligson could provide a spark to their struggle against the Empire, and at first he indicated that he was inclined to help. Ostensibly for the Grohl Liberation Front's war effort, Kligson constructed a massive [[Space station/Legends|space station]] dubbed "[[Kligson's Moon/Legends|Kligson's Moon]]"<ref name="EGWAC8" /> out of [[Starship/Legends|starship]] parts and [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] [[Engine/Legends|engines]].<ref name="cynabar">''[[Cynabar's Fantastic Technology: Droids]]''</ref> But gradually Kligson's behavior became more erratic and distant, and he began to shun the Grohl Liberation Front's organic representatives and instead demand [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]] be sent in their place. After a few months, Kligson fired up his [[Moon/Legends|moon's]] engines and blasted to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], leaving his home behind for good.<ref name="EGWAC8" />

Kligson retreated from organic company completely in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to come, and Kligson's Moon&mdash;often referred to simply as "[[Droid/Legends|Droid]] World"&mdash;became its own society populated only by droids and other machines. Kligson ran the droid civilization with the help of his chief [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]], [[Z-X3|Zee-Exthree]], a rejected experimental Imperial battle droid Kligson reclaimed.<ref name="marvel47" /> Kligson's Moon became a popular legend among [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]], who told of a reclusive tinkerer who could seemingly do anything with machines. A few managed to track Kligson down and speak with him, including the droid researcher [[Simonelle]], but outside of the droids he lived with he refused to consort with any unless they could bring him a new challenge in droid design.<ref name="EGWAC8" /> In Kligson's mechanical realm, visitors abided by two ironclad rules: no organic was allowed to set foot on his moon, and anything Kligson repaired, he kept.<ref name="marvel47" />

===Civil war===
{{Quote|I've been ''through'' a war. I was able to provide more... ''practical''... programming than Zee-Exthree... but at such a ''price,'' my friends... and such a terrible ''waste.''|Kligson|<ref name="marvel47" />}}
[[File:SuchATerribleWaste.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Kligson is overcome with emotion after the demise of Zee-Exthree.]]
One such event happened in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], when [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] got his hands on a damaged [[Imperial warbot]] which frustrated him in his efforts to reconstruct a full schematic. Skywalker sought out Kligson upon a recommendation from a Rebel soldier who had heard of the "Droid World," and intrigued by the challenge of reconstructing the warbot, Kligson consented to allow Skywalker's personal droids, [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], to come aboard his moon and record Kligson's work on the Imperial machine. Although Kligson had cause to detest the Imperials, the cyborg had kept his society as far from the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] as possible, and wanted nothing to do with the conflict between the Rebels and the Empire. By this time, however, Zee-Exthree had assembled a faction of droids that supported the Empire, and sought to use the warbot to depose Kligson and take over his moon in the Emperor's name.<ref name="marvel47" />

Kligson had begun to suspect Zee-Exthree's treachery, and had taken the precaution of commissioning a [[Kligson's android duplicate|replica droid]] to act in his name. By the time Skywalker arrived at his station, he had realized that he needed something dramatic to draw Zee-Exthree out. Kligson felt that the presence of two Rebel droids could be exactly what he needed, and his intuition proved correct. Zee-Exthree and his faction launched an attempt to depose Kligson and take the moon in the Empire's name, and destroyed Kligson's replica in the process. However, Kligson still had the upper hand. Kligson had the [[Kligson's faction|faction]] of droids that still remained loyal to him repair Skywalker's Imperial warbot and unleash it against Zee-Exthree and his army. Kligson proved victorious in the [[Kligson's Moon civil war|power struggle]], and afterward fired up his station's engines and retreated deeper into [[Realspace/Legends|space]] ahead of Imperial pursuit.<ref name="marvel47" />

After leaving Skywalker's droids behind, Kligson and his Droid World once again became a spacer legend, with only occasional rumors surfacing in the years to come.<ref name="EGWAC8" /> During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] over two decades after Kligson's encounter with Skywalker, Kligson's Moon came under [[Attack on Kligson's Moon|attack]] from the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. However, Kligson's realm was saved by intervention from the [[Iron Knight]]s, a band of [[Shard (species)|Shard]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] encased within droid bodies.<ref name="hyperspace">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/81/indexp7.html|text=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena|int=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|But I have two rules in my world. First, that no human set foot on my planet. And second, anything I repair I keep.|Kligson to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="further" />}}
A dyed-in-the-wool warrior from his early years, Kligson's betrayal at the hands of his Imperial masters prompted a radical personality shift that distanced him from all other organic life. Physically imposing with [[Holodrama/Legends|holo]] idol good looks, Kligson was, above all else, a Sucharmese patriot, stirred to defend his homeworld after feeling deep disgust at the sight of Trade Federation [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] on his native soil. And although he was an enthusiastic supporter of the New Order and the Galactic Empire he served, Kligson's loyalties lay with his homeworld, and he was marked for death after questioning orders that would have had him leading an Imperial invasion of Sucharme.<ref name="EGWAC8" />

Disenchanted by his traumatic experiences across a lifetime of war, Kligson vowed to never interact with organics again, finding solace in his new mechanical brethren&mdash;however, with great convincing, he would deign to speak with other organics with cybernetic limbs,<ref name="cynabar" /> or ones who could give him a new challenge in droid design. Renowned as a master mechanic, Kligson's aptitude with droids soon became spacer legend.<ref name="EGWAC8" /> Droids became Kligson's life during his years on "Droid World," and he was especially fascinated by mechanicals that consented to living under organic masters. Although the Empire had nearly killed him, Kligson refused to take sides in the Galactic Civil War, renouncing the "taint of war" that he believed both sides of the war spread to more logical machines. His resolve only deepened after the civil war aboard Kligson's Moon, pushing him further away from organic life.<ref name="marvel47" /> In his cyborg form, Kligson required neither food nor [[Water/Legends|water]], and his augmentations included [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] built into his hands.<ref name="cynabar" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Kligson-record_version.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An alternate Kligson as seen in ''The Further Adventures: Droid World'']]
Kligson first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 47|''Star Wars'' (1977) 47]], written by [[Archie Goodwin]] and released in [[1981]]. In the comic, Kligson was illustrated by [[Carmine Infantino]]<ref name="marvel47" />&mdash;he was also pictured by [[Dick Foes]] in the book-and-record ''[[The Further Adventures: Droid World]]'', which portrayed his cybernetic enhancements slightly differently.<ref name="further" /> Kligson's backstory was finally provided in [[2014]], when [[Jason Fry]] devoted a section of the [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|
''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]] to his story.<ref name="EGWAC8" />
